title: The Tomb, the Bank, and the Senate Seat: Prescott Bush from Columbus to Putnam Cemetery
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Columbus, Middletown, and the Tomb on High Street

stops.name: Columbus, Ohio, birth in the ironmaster's house
stops.date_confidence: attested; the year is given in the Wikipedia article, the full date 15 May 1895 is the standard biographical date and is not itself quoted in the fetched text
stops.campa: Prescott Sheldon Bush is born in Columbus to Samuel Prescott Bush, a railroad and steel executive, and to Flora Sheldon Bush. The Ohio the family holds is made of foundries and rolling stock: money in iron, not yet money in paper. Nothing in the birth record marks what will come out of this house, a United States senator, a president, a second president, and a New York bank seized in wartime by the government he will serve. He carries his father's name and his mother's, and he will pass both of them down.
suggested_refs: Samuel Prescott Bush's Columbus industrial career, background to the birth

stops.name: Middletown, Rhode Island, the Episcopal boarding school
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span 1908 to 1913; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He is sent east at thirteen to St. George's School on Aquidneck Island, an Episcopal boarding school above the Newport shore, and stays five years. The Ohio accent is filed off here. What replaces it is the accent of a class that does not have to explain itself: chapel twice a day, Latin, games, and the assumption that the boys in the room will know each other for the rest of their lives. He learns to sing. The school hands him on to Yale in 1913 with no gap between the two.
suggested_refs: St. George's School, 372 Purgatory Road, Middletown, Rhode Island
sources: Wikipedia, 'St. George's School (Rhode Island)' for the school's coordinates

stops.name: New Haven, Yale College and the Whiffenpoofs
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span 1913 to 1917; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He enrolls at Yale and takes what the college has to give: Zeta Psi, the Whiffenpoofs, the presidency of the Glee Club, varsity golf and varsity baseball. He is six foot four and sings bass, and the singing matters more to him than anyone expects, lasting past the war and past the Senate. New Haven becomes the family's second town. His son will come here, and his grandson, and a great-grandson, until the walk from Chapel Street to the Old Campus is a piece of inherited property like the house in Greenwich.
suggested_refs: Yale Glee Club and Whiffenpoof records, classes of 1913 to 1917
sources: canonical New Haven pin inherited from ron_rivest.journey.json and john_von_neumann.journey.json

stops.name: Cold Spring Harbor, New York, the Eugenics Record Office
stops.date_confidence: attested for the institution and its funding; Prescott Bush is not placed here by any source and is a Yale undergraduate in this year
stops.campa: While Bush is singing bass in New Haven, Alexander Graham Bell chairs the board of the Eugenics Record Office at Cold Spring Harbor, founded in 1910 on Harriman, Rockefeller and Carnegie money. The Harriman share comes from Mary Williamson Harriman, whose sons Averell and Roland will be Bush's banking partners within fifteen years and whose firm will carry his name to Wall Street. Bush is not here and no source puts him here. The money is here, and so is the argument about heredity he will fund from the other end thirty years later.
suggested_refs: Eugenics Record Office founding papers, Cold Spring Harbor, 1910
sources: Wikipedia, 'Prescott Bush' for the later Harriman partnership

stops.name: New Haven, tapped for Skull and Bones
stops.date_confidence: attested as membership; the tap date is conventional and not given in the sources reached
stops.campa: In his senior spring he is taken into Skull and Bones, the windowless brownstone tomb at 64 High Street where fifteen men a year are made into a club that outlasts the college. His son will be tapped, and his grandson after that, so that for three generations a Bush walks up these steps in the dark. Everything the society is later accused of reaches him through this door, including a skull said to have been carried back from an army post in Oklahoma the following year.
suggested_refs: The Skull and Bones tomb, 64 High Street, New Haven
sources: Wikipedia, 'Skull and Bones' (street address given, no coordinates published)

segments.name: The Guns in France and the Skull at Fort Sill

stops.name: Verdun, the intelligence course
stops.date_confidence: attested that the training happened at Verdun; the month is not given in the sources reached
stops.campa: A captain of field artillery in the American Expeditionary Forces, he is sent to Verdun for intelligence training and attached for a period to a staff of French officers. The ground he is taught on has already eaten a generation of two armies. He learns to read a map for what is hidden on it, to estimate a battery he cannot see, and to write down what he has inferred as though it were known. The same habit serves him afterward in rooms where the important holdings are the ones kept off the letterhead, and he will sit in those rooms for forty years.
suggested_refs: American Expeditionary Forces intelligence training at Verdun, 1918

stops.name: The Meuse-Argonne front, under fire
stops.date_confidence: attested for the offensive and his presence in it; the date given is the opening of the offensive, not a date attached to him personally
stops.campa: He goes into the Meuse-Argonne with the 158th Field Artillery Brigade, the largest battle the United States Army has ever fought, and comes under fire in it. He is twenty-three. Whatever he saw he does not later trade on: there is no war book, no campaign speech built on the Argonne, no medal narrative that outlives him. The war gives him a captaincy and a habit of command, and it gives him the plain fact that he was there. That fact is a credential a banker can spend for the next forty years without once saying it aloud.
suggested_refs: 158th Field Artillery Brigade records, Meuse-Argonne offensive

stops.name: Fort Sill, Oklahoma, the grave in the legend
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction and disputed: the Mead letter is dated only to 1918, the month is unknown, and Bush himself is in France for most of that year, which is one argument against his personal involvement; the stop is placed late in 1918 for ordering only
stops.campa: A story attaches itself to him here and never comes off. Skull and Bones men serving at the Fort Sill artillery post are said to have dug up Geronimo's skull and carried it to New Haven, and a 1918 letter from Winter Mead to F. Trubee Davison records the skull as safe inside the Tomb. Mead was not at Fort Sill and could not have watched anything. Geronimo's grave was unmarked in 1918. Bush is in France for most of that year. The story survives all of it, because the men it names are the kind of men about whom such a story wants to be true.
stops.quote: The skull of the worthy Geronimo the Terrible, exhumed from its tomb at Fort Sill by your club... is now safe inside the [Tomb].
stops.quote_source: Winter Mead, letter to F. Trubee Davison, 1918, quoted in Wikipedia, 'Geronimo,' via Marc Wortman
suggested_refs: Geronimo's grave at the Fort Sill Apache Prisoner of War Cemetery

stops.name: St. Louis, Missouri, the hardware company
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Discharged, he goes to work for the Simmons Hardware Company in St. Louis, selling into the middle of the country. It is the only stretch of his life spent at ordinary work in an ordinary city, and it lasts two years. What ends it is not a promotion. It is a wedding in Maine, and a father-in-law who is president of a New York investment house and has a use for a son-in-law who is presentable, disciplined, and already known to every man who matters from New Haven and from the war.
suggested_refs: Simmons Hardware Company, St. Louis, employment records 1919 to 1921

segments.name: The Walker Marriage and the Rubber Years

stops.name: Kennebunkport, Maine, marriage to Dorothy Walker
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date of the marriage; the ceremony's venue is disputed and the pin is Walker's Point, the estate, not a confirmed wedding site
stops.campa: He marries Dorothy Walker on the sixth of August. Her father, George Herbert Walker, bought this granite point in 1902 and builds a smaller house on it as a wedding gift to the couple, which is not the same thing as holding the wedding here: the ceremony is generally placed at the Episcopal church in the village. Everything Prescott Bush later has flows through this marriage: the bank, the pension, the house, the name he gives his second son, and the point itself, which the family will keep for a hundred years.
suggested_refs: Walker's Point Estate, Kennebunkport, bought by George Herbert Walker in 1902
sources: Wikipedia, 'Walker's Point Estate' for coordinates and the wedding-gift house

stops.name: South Braintree, Massachusetts, president of sales
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; day defaulted
stops.campa: After a short return to Columbus and a few months at Hupp Products, he becomes president of sales for Stedman Products, a rubber-goods manufacturer in South Braintree. He is twenty-eight and selling floor mats. The village is three years past the payroll robbery that hanged Sacco and Vanzetti, and the trial is still running while he works here, though no source connects him to it. His first son is already born. His second will be born up the road within the year.
suggested_refs: Stedman Products Company, South Braintree, Massachusetts
sources: Wikipedia, 'Braintree, Massachusetts' for the corrected village coordinates

stops.name: Milton, Massachusetts, 173 Adams Street
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In a house on Milton Hill, on the road that runs down toward the Neponset and the Quincy line, Dorothy Bush gives birth to a second son and they name him George Herbert Walker Bush after her father. Prescott Bush is a rubber salesman living in a rented Massachusetts town. Sixty-five years later the boy born in this room will take the oath as president of the United States, and twelve years after that his own son will take it again. The address is now the only reason anyone remembers the house.
suggested_refs: 173 Adams Street, Milton Hill, Milton, Massachusetts
sources: Wikipedia, 'Milton, Massachusetts' for the address and the birth date

stops.name: Greenwich, Connecticut, the family seat
stops.date_confidence: disputed: the Wikipedia article on George H. W. Bush gives 1925 with the move to United States Rubber, while other entries in this dossier give 1926 with the move to W. A. Harriman; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He joins United States Rubber as manager of its foreign division and moves the household to Greenwich, forty minutes by train from Wall Street and a world away from Braintree. Here the family stops moving. Five children are raised in this town, three of them born after the move; he will sit in its town meeting for seventeen years, win its club championships, be buried in its cemetery. Every later address, Washington, Manhattan, Kennebunkport, Fishers Island, is measured from this one.
suggested_refs: The Bush household in Greenwich, Connecticut, from 1925
sources: Wikipedia, 'George H. W. Bush' for the 1925 date

segments.name: Wall Street: Harriman, Brown Brothers, Union Banking

stops.name: Wall Street, vice-president of W. A. Harriman and Co.
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: His father-in-law is president of W. A. Harriman and Co., and Bush becomes vice-president of it. He is thirty-one and has never worked in a bank. The firm lends into Germany, Poland, and the Soviet Union in the decade when American capital is the only capital rebuilding Europe, and it does so through holding companies whose beneficial owners are recorded in Rotterdam and Berlin rather than in New York. He is good at the work. He will stay in the same partnership, under two names, for thirty-six years.
suggested_refs: W. A. Harriman and Co., New York, 1926 partnership records

stops.name: 59 Wall Street, partner at Brown Brothers Harriman
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the merger; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Brown Brothers and Co. merges with W. A. Harriman and Co. and Bush becomes a partner of the house that results, alongside Averell and Roland Harriman. It is the largest private bank in the country and it is a farm for public men: Averell Harriman will be governor of New York and one of the Wise Men whom Clark Clifford watches turn against the Vietnam war in 1968. William Casey will work the same downtown blocks a generation later on his way to the SEC and the CIA. Bush keeps the partnership for thirty-one years.
suggested_refs: Brown Brothers Harriman and Co., 59 Wall Street, partnership of 1931

stops.name: Lower Manhattan, director of the Union Banking Corporation
stops.date_confidence: disputed: Wikipedia calls him a founder and one of seven directors of a corporation incorporated in 1924, which is two years before he joined W. A. Harriman; the documentary record of the seizure supports 1934; the conflict is left standing
stops.campa: He sits as one of seven directors of the Union Banking Corporation and holds one of its four thousand shares. The corporation is a New York shell whose stock is held on behalf of a Rotterdam bank, and behind the Rotterdam bank stands Fritz Thyssen, the Ruhr steel magnate who paid into the National Socialist party in its lean years. Bush signs nothing that says any of this. He is a director of a bank, which is a thing a Wall Street partner is, on a board where his firm's business needs an American name.
suggested_refs: Union Banking Corporation certificate of incorporation and director lists
sources: canonical Wall Street pin from alexander_hamilton.journey.json:330 and george_washington.journey.json:460

stops.name: Rotterdam, the Bank voor Handel en Scheepvaart
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the bank and its Thyssen tie are attested for the 1930s, no source places Prescott Bush in Rotterdam, and the year is a placeholder inside the decade chosen to keep the stop in sequence
stops.campa: The parent of the New York shell keeps its books here, in a Dutch port city, which is the whole point of it: German money that is legally Dutch, moving through a neutral kingdom into an American bank. Fritz Thyssen's own credit runs through the Cologne and Ruhr houses that Salomon Oppenheim's descendants built. His half-brother Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza spends the same decade buying pictures, among them the Caravaggio of Saint Catherine of Alexandria now in Madrid. No source puts Bush on this quay. His signature is on the other end of the wire.
suggested_refs: Bank voor Handel en Scheepvaart, Rotterdam, holding structure of the 1930s

stops.name: New York City, Hitler's Angel in the morning paper
stops.date_confidence: attested for the article; the newspaper is contested, see quote_source, and the pin is a generic Manhattan point, not a located newsroom
stops.campa: Five months before Pearl Harbor a reporter traces Fritz Thyssen's American money to a New York bank and prints it on the front page. Wikipedia credits the Washington Post; a full reproduction of the article credits M. J. Racusin of the New York Herald Tribune, dated the thirtieth of July 1941; the Guardian in 2004 credits the Herald-Tribune but words the headline differently and gives 1942. The story is real and the paper it ran in is not settled. Prescott Bush is a director of the bank in question and is not named in it.
stops.quote: Hitler's Angel has 3 millions in N.Y. Bank
stops.quote_source: M. J. Racusin, New York Herald Tribune, 30 July 1941, per the reproduced article text; Wikipedia, 'Union Banking Corporation' attributes the same headline to the Washington Post, and the Guardian of 25 September 2004 renders it 'Hitler's Angel Has $3m in US Bank' and dates it 1942
suggested_refs: The original front page of 30 July 1941, not located in this research pass
sources: rapeutation.com reproduction of the Racusin article

stops.name: Washington, D.C., the Alien Property Custodian's report
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date of the report; the coordinate is a generic downtown Washington point, no sourced office address was found
stops.campa: The Office of Alien Property Custodian files its report on the Union Banking Corporation. An earlier investigator had already written that he could not establish who owned the Dutch bank. The 1942 report says the same thing about the money itself, in the same flat voice, and the government seizes the bank anyway. The state is not claiming to have proved that Fritz Thyssen owns these funds. It is claiming that in a war it does not have to know before it acts. The claim outlives the war by a good deal.
stops.quote: Whether any or all part of the funds held by Union Banking Corporation, or companies associated with it, belong to Fritz Thyssen could not be established in this investigation.
stops.quote_source: Office of Alien Property Custodian report on Union Banking Corporation, 5 October 1942, quoted in Wikipedia, 'Union Banking Corporation'
suggested_refs: Office of Alien Property Custodian investigative file, Union Banking Corporation, 1941 to 1942

stops.name: Lower Manhattan, the bank seized under the Trading with the Enemy Act
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; Vesting Order No. 248 is generally dated 20 October 1942, while Wikipedia gives no seizure date at all and cites only the 5 October report
stops.campa: Vesting Order No. 248 takes the Union Banking Corporation into the custody of the United States for the duration of the war. Prescott Bush's one share goes with it, along with the other three thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine. He is not charged, not called, not named in the order; the assets come back after the war and the partnership continues without a break. Hugo Boss is cutting party uniforms in Metzingen the same month, and the war still has nearly three years to run.
suggested_refs: Vesting Order No. 248, Office of Alien Property Custodian, October 1942

segments.name: Greenwich, the Clubs, and the League

stops.name: Round Hill Club, Greenwich, the club championships
stops.date_confidence: attested that he was a multi-year club champion; the specific years are not given in the sources reached, and the date stands for the period
stops.campa: He wins the club championship at Round Hill more than once, and golf turns out to be the through-line of his public life: the Yale varsity, this course, the national governing body, and finally a standing invitation from a president. In Greenwich the game is not recreation, it is the committee room. Deals, endorsements, and the succession of local offices are settled in fourballs on this hill, and a very tall man who sings and does not lose gets asked to serve on things.
suggested_refs: Round Hill Club, Greenwich, club championship records of the 1920s and 1930s

stops.name: New York City, president of the United States Golf Association
stops.date_confidence: attested: Wikipedia gives him the offices of secretary, vice-president and president in succession across 1928 to 1935, the presidency being the last of the three; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He rises through the United States Golf Association from secretary to vice-president to president, seven years of committee work ending in the top chair in 1935. It is a national office with no politics in it, which is exactly its value: it makes a New York banker into a name that appears in newspapers in states he has never worked in, attached to nothing but a game. Fifteen years later, when he runs for the Senate, the columnists will report that nobody knows Mr. Bush.
suggested_refs: United States Golf Association officer lists, 1928 to 1935

stops.name: Greenwich, moderator of the Representative Town Meeting
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: he is generally reported as moderator for about seventeen years from the mid 1930s, but the Wikipedia article on Prescott Bush contains nothing about Greenwich town government and no source reached in this pass fixes the start year
stops.campa: He takes the chair of the Greenwich Representative Town Meeting and keeps it for something like seventeen years. It is the smallest office he ever holds and the one that teaches him the trade: recognizing speakers, counting a room, ruling on a point of order without making an enemy, week after week, in a town where the people arguing are also the people he banks with and plays with. When he reaches the Senate at fifty-seven he has already run more meetings than most senators ever will.
suggested_refs: Greenwich Representative Town Meeting minute books, 1930s to 1950
sources: General biographical accounts; the cited Wikipedia article does not support this entry and the gap is flagged in the report

stops.name: New York, the American Birth Control League
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of his involvement; the location is inferred from the League's New York headquarters and is not itself sourced
stops.campa: In the same year the government seizes his bank, he becomes involved with the American Birth Control League. The organization renames itself Planned Parenthood that year and spends the next decades separating its argument from the heredity science that funded the Cold Spring Harbor office when he was an undergraduate. Bush comes to it as a fundraiser, which is what he is. The connection will cost him an election eight years later, when a broadcast names him on the eve of the vote.
suggested_refs: American Birth Control League records, 1942, the year of its renaming

stops.name: New Haven, member of the Yale Corporation
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span 1944 to 1956; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He joins the Yale Corporation, the university's governing board, and sits on it for twelve years. He has already founded the Yale Glee Club Associates in 1937 to keep the singing funded. From this chair he helps govern the institution that took him at eighteen, will take his son, and will take his grandson, while the tomb on High Street goes on tapping fifteen men a year two streets from where the board meets. He leaves the board in 1956, four years into his own time in the Senate.
suggested_refs: Yale Corporation membership rolls, 1944 to 1956
sources: canonical New Haven pin inherited from ron_rivest.journey.json

stops.name: New Haven, the grandson born
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: George Walker Bush is born in New Haven while his father, back from flying torpedo bombers in the Pacific, finishes at Yale on the accelerated postwar schedule. Prescott Bush is fifty-one, a partner at Brown Brothers Harriman, a member of the Corporation of the university the child is born beside. The boy will be Governor of Texas and, in 2001, President of the United States, the second of this line. Three generations of the family are alive in this town in this year, and all three are Bonesmen.
suggested_refs: Grace-New Haven Hospital birth record, 6 July 1946
sources: canonical New Haven pin inherited from ron_rivest.journey.json

stops.name: New York, treasurer of the first Planned Parenthood campaign
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the location is inferred from the organization's New York headquarters and is not itself sourced
stops.campa: He serves as treasurer of the first nationwide fundraising campaign Planned Parenthood ever runs, and in the same year takes the finance chairmanship of the Connecticut Republican party. The two jobs are the same job: he is the man who asks rich men for money and gets it. In 1947 no one in his party thinks these two chairmanships sit oddly together. Within a single generation the arrangement becomes unthinkable, and his son will spend a career explaining a position his father held without needing to explain it.
suggested_refs: Planned Parenthood Federation of America, first national campaign, 1947

stops.name: Connecticut, the eleven hundred and two votes
stops.date_confidence: attested for the election and the margin; the date given is the general election day of 1950
stops.campa: In his first run for the Senate he loses the special election to William Benton by one thousand one hundred and two votes out of eight hundred and sixty thousand. Drew Pearson broadcasts his Planned Parenthood connection days before the vote; the campaign blames the loss on it. Westbrook Pegler, syndicated in papers Bush will never read, has already filed the sentence that the whole state seems to agree with, and the second half of it is truer at that moment than the first.
stops.quote: is coming on to be known as President Truman's Harry Hopkins. Nobody knows Mr. Bush and he hasn't a Chinaman's chance.
stops.quote_source: Westbrook Pegler, syndicated column on the 1950 Connecticut Senate campaign, Burlington Daily News-Times, 22 August 1950, quoted in Wikipedia, 'Prescott Bush'; the period racial slur is reproduced verbatim per house rule
suggested_refs: Connecticut Senate special election returns, 1950

stops.name: Connecticut, the special election won
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Two years later the seat comes open again by death and he wins it, beating Abraham Ribicoff on the same day Dwight Eisenhower carries the state and the country. He is fifty-seven years old and has never held an office larger than a town meeting chair. Because it is a special election he is sworn in at once rather than in January, which puts him in the chamber for the last weeks of the Truman presidency and gives him seniority over the whole incoming class elected with him.
suggested_refs: Connecticut Senate special election returns, 4 November 1952

stops.name: Washington, D.C., the seat in the Capitol
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the pool gives the election date and the end of the term, 3 January 1963, but no swearing-in date; the day after the special election is the conventional assumption and is not attested here
stops.campa: He takes his seat as a senator from Connecticut. The Wall Street partnership goes on leave, not into liquidation. He is one of the tallest men in the chamber and sings in the Senate quartet, and he arrives with a rolodex no freshman has ever arrived with: thirty-one years of Brown Brothers Harriman clients, a national golf constituency, and a president who wants a fourth for the weekend. Ten years and two months from this day he will walk back out and the family will not leave Washington again for forty.
suggested_refs: Congressional Biographical Directory entry for Prescott Bush, inaccessible in this pass

stops.name: The Senate floor, the censure of Joseph McCarthy
stops.date_confidence: attested for the vote and the date; the wording of the floor remarks is known through Time magazine and has not been checked against the Congressional Record
stops.campa: He votes with the sixty-seven to censure Joseph McCarthy, and he speaks first. Twenty-two senators vote the other way, and the Republicans in the chamber split down the middle. It is the least characteristic thing he ever does, a banker with two years of seniority standing up to say aloud what the men around him are saying in cloakrooms, and it is the reason his name survives in Senate histories that have no interest in Union Banking or Greenwich or golf.
stops.quote: caused dangerous divisions among the American people because of his attitude and the attitude he has encouraged among his followers: that there can be no honest differences of opinion with him. Either you must follow Senator McCarthy blindly, not daring to express any doubts or disagreements about any of his actions, or, in his eyes, you must be a Communist, a Communist sympathizer, or a fool who has been duped by the Communist line.
stops.quote_source: Prescott Bush, Senate floor remarks in the censure debate, 2 December 1954, as quoted in Time, 13 December 1954, relayed by Wikipedia, 'Prescott Bush'
suggested_refs: Congressional Record, 2 December 1954, censure debate, not retrieved in this pass

stops.name: Augusta National, a fourth for the president
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the friendship and the golf are widely reported in secondary Bush-family biographies, not confirmed in the Wikipedia extract used, and no specific round at Augusta is dated in the sources reached
stops.campa: He plays with Eisenhower, at Augusta and wherever else the president is, and by the middle of the decade he is a regular in the White House social circle as well. Thirty years of golf administration turn out to have been an apprenticeship for this. His influence is not committee power and it is not oratory. It is the standing invitation. A senator who can be telephoned on a Saturday morning is a senator whose views on a bill are heard on the tee, in shirtsleeves, before they are ever heard in a hearing room by a man taking notes.
suggested_refs: Eisenhower's golfing calendar, Augusta National, 1953 to 1961
sources: Secondary Bush-family biographies; not confirmed in the Wikipedia article on Prescott Bush

stops.name: Connecticut, re-elected with fifty-five percent
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the share; the date given is the general election day of 1956, and the pool names Thomas J. Dodd as the opponent in one lens without confirmation elsewhere
stops.campa: He wins a full six-year term with fifty-five percent of the vote, running behind Eisenhower in his own state but comfortably ahead of the man from Hartford. The Connecticut he now represents is insurance, brass, submarines and Yale, and he votes for the interstates, for civil rights bills that die in committee, and for the defense budget of a president he golfs with. He is sixty-one and has finally, twenty-five years after Wall Street made him rich, become a public man on his own paper.
suggested_refs: Connecticut Senate general election returns, 1956

stops.name: Washington, D.C., the piece for Reader's Digest
stops.date_confidence: attested for the publication and month; only the title was retrievable in this pass and the pin is his Senate office, not a place of composition
stops.campa: He publishes in Reader's Digest, the magazine that sits in every dentist's waiting room in the country, under a title that is an argument in itself. The year is 1959: Khrushchev is coming to Iowa, the missile gap is being invented, and a senator who spent the twenties lending American money into Germany and the Soviet Union now tells eleven million households that peace is a function of visible strength. The body of the article could not be retrieved. The title was doing most of the work anyway.
stops.quote: To Preserve Peace Let's Show the Russians How Strong We Are!
stops.quote_source: Prescott Bush, article title, Reader's Digest, July 1959, listed in the Writings section of Wikipedia, 'Prescott Bush'
suggested_refs: Reader's Digest, July 1959, full article text, not retrieved in this pass

stops.name: Washington, D.C., the term ends
stops.date_confidence: attested; the decision not to seek re-election is attested to 1962 without a month
stops.campa: In 1962 he declines to run again, citing his health, and on the third of January 1963 his term ends. He is sixty-seven and has been a senator for ten years and two months. The seat passes to Abraham Ribicoff, the man he beat for it in 1952, which closes the account exactly. His son is in Texas drilling for oil and about to lose his own first race. That son will spend the next twenty-six years climbing toward an office the father never ran for, and will name him, in campaign after campaign, as the standard he is being measured against.
suggested_refs: Senate service record of Prescott Bush, 1952 to 1963

segments.name: Fishers Island, Walker's Point, and Putnam Cemetery

stops.name: Fishers Island, New York, the other house
stops.date_confidence: attested that the family kept a house here; no dates are given in the sources reached and the year stands for the middle of the century
stops.campa: The family keeps a house on Fishers Island, seven miles off the Connecticut shore and reachable only by the ferry out of New London, alongside Greenwich, Manhattan and Kennebunkport. It is a small place with a golf course, no bridge, and a membership that overlaps his club in Greenwich and his class at Yale. The geography of this life is a closed circuit of four or five addresses, and the men he meets inside it are the same men at every one of them, in different weather.
suggested_refs: The Bush family house on Fishers Island, New York

stops.name: Walker's Point, Kennebunkport, the summers
stops.date_confidence: attested as a lifelong pattern; no single summer is dated in the sources reached and the year is a placeholder within the span
stops.campa: He summers on the point his father-in-law bought in 1902, as he has since the year he married, and the grandchildren learn to fish off the same rocks. The estate outlasts him by generations: it becomes the summer White House of one president and the burial ground of the family's public image, the place American television goes when it wants to show what this family is. He is the link in the chain that carried it from the Walkers to the Bushes, and he did it by getting married.
